# Into R: a first look with DESeq2 {#sec-into-r}

The processing ends with gene-level counts: the `tximport` object, from a
pipeline or from your own Salmon runs. This chapter picks them up in R and
takes the first steps of a differential expression analysis with **DESeq2**.
It's an introduction, not a full statistics course. The
[DESeq2 vignette](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html)
is the reference.

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false, "flowchart": {"htmlLabels": false}}}%%
flowchart LR
  Q["Salmon quant.sf<br/>(one folder per sample)"] --> A["Option A<br/>tximport"] --> D1["DESeqDataSetFromTximport()"]
  Q --> B["Option B<br/>tximeta + summarizeToGene"] --> D2["DESeqDataSet()"]
  R["pipeline's<br/>_tximport.rds"] -.-> D1
  D1 & D2 --> DDS["dds"] --> P["PCA<br/>(check samples)"] --> T["DESeq() → results()"] --> O["table of genes:<br/>log2FC, padj"]
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What to expect from the practice data

The practice set has two donors, untreated vs dexamethasone, and only 500,000
read pairs per sample (with the `chr22` references, a few thousand counted
reads). That's enough to **learn every step**, but not for reliable
statistics. Run the same code on the full airway dataset (see
[download-public-data](https://jpflores-13.github.io/download-public-data/chapters/worked-example.html))
or your own data for real results.
:::

## Setup

Use the `rnaseq-r` conda environment (`conda activate rnaseq-r`, then `R`),
or any R ≥ 4.3 / RStudio with:

```r
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("DESeq2", "tximport", "tximeta", "GenomicFeatures", "rtracklayer", "apeglm"))
```

Start R from a terminal where you ran `source $WALK/env.sh`, so
`Sys.getenv("WALK")` and `Sys.getenv("GTF")` work. In RStudio, replace those
with the actual paths.

## Describe the samples

DESeq2 needs a table with one row per sample and the variables you want to
compare. For the practice data:

```r
library(DESeq2)

walk    <- Sys.getenv("WALK")                       # e.g. "~/omics-walkthru-practice"
samples <- c("N61311_untrt", "N61311_dex", "N052611_untrt", "N052611_dex")
coldata <- data.frame(
  row.names = samples,
  donor     = factor(sub("_.*", "", samples)),
  treatment = factor(sub(".*_", "", samples), levels = c("untrt", "dex"))   # first level = reference
)
coldata
```

The **first level** of `treatment` (`untrt`) is the reference: fold changes
are reported as `dex` relative to `untrt`.

## Option A: tximport

```r
library(tximport)
library(GenomicFeatures)

files <- file.path(walk, "work", "quant", samples, "quant.sf")
names(files) <- samples
txdb    <- makeTxDbFromGFF(Sys.getenv("GTF"), format = "gtf")
tx2gene <- select(txdb, keys = keys(txdb, "GENEID"), keytype = "GENEID", columns = "TXNAME")[, 2:1]
txi     <- tximport(files, type = "salmon", tx2gene = tx2gene)

stopifnot(identical(rownames(coldata), colnames(txi$counts)))
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromTximport(txi, colData = coldata, design = ~ donor + treatment)
```

`DESeqDataSetFromTximport` takes the counts (rounded to whole numbers) and
uses `txi$length` as a per-gene, per-sample offset ([tximport](tximport.qmd)).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Coming from a pipeline's `_tximport.rds` (e.g. bagPipes RNApipe)

```r
txi <- readRDS("output/quant/<runName>_tximport.rds")
ss  <- read.delim("output/<runName>_RNApipeSamplesheet.txt", na.strings = "")
## bagPipes' current txImporter.R leaves column names as NA; the order is the samplesheet's
for (m in c("counts", "abundance", "length")) colnames(txi[[m]]) <- ss$sn
```

Then build `coldata` from the columns of `ss` (one row per `ss$sn`, same order).
:::

## Option B: tximeta {#option-b-start-from-tximeta}

```r
library(tximeta)

cd <- data.frame(files = file.path(walk, "work", "quant", samples, "quant.sf"),
                 names = samples, coldata)
se  <- tximeta(cd)            # if it says the index is unknown, see "linked transcriptomes"
gse <- summarizeToGene(se)
dds <- DESeqDataSet(gse, design = ~ donor + treatment)
```

The practice `chr22` index is a custom transcriptome, so tximeta won't
recognise it until you link it ([tximeta](tximport.qmd#tximeta)). The bonus of
this route: `rowRanges(dds)` holds every gene's coordinates.

## Filter, then look before you test

```r
dds <- dds[rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= 2, ]      # drop genes with almost no reads
nrow(dds)

vsd <- if (nrow(dds) >= 1000) vst(dds, blind = TRUE) else varianceStabilizingTransformation(dds, blind = TRUE)
plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = c("treatment", "donor"))
```

Samples should separate by treatment or by donor. Often donor dominates in
primary cells, which is exactly why the design includes `donor`. If a sample
sits somewhere unexpected, check the sample table before anything else.

## Test

```r
dds <- DESeq(dds)
resultsNames(dds)                     # includes "treatment_dex_vs_untrt"
res <- results(dds, name = "treatment_dex_vs_untrt", alpha = 0.05)
summary(res)

resLFC <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = "treatment_dex_vs_untrt", type = "apeglm")   # shrunken fold changes
plotMA(resLFC, ylim = c(-5, 5))
```

`design = ~ donor + treatment` compares dex with untreated **within each
donor**, so differences between donors don't drown out the drug effect.

| Column of `res` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `baseMean` | Average normalised count across all samples |
| `log2FoldChange` | log2(dex / untrt): 1 = doubled, −1 = halved |
| `lfcSE` | Its standard error |
| `pvalue` | Raw p-value |
| `padj` | **Adjusted p-value** (Benjamini–Hochberg). Use this one; `NA` means the gene was filtered out (too low or an outlier) |

## Add gene names and save

```r
gtf   <- rtracklayer::import(Sys.getenv("GTF"))
genes <- unique(as.data.frame(gtf[gtf$type == "gene"])[, c("gene_id", "gene_name", "gene_type")])

out <- as.data.frame(resLFC)
out$gene_id <- rownames(out)
out <- merge(genes, out, by = "gene_id")
out <- out[order(out$padj), ]
write.csv(out, "DE_dex_vs_untrt.csv", row.names = FALSE)
head(out[, c("gene_name", "log2FoldChange", "padj")], 20)
```

With the full airway dataset, well-known dexamethasone-responsive genes such as
*FKBP5*, *TSC22D3* and *PER1* go up strongly. With the practice subset, check
whether any of them appear (they're not on chr22).

## Where to go next

- **One gene**: `plotCounts(dds, gene = "ENSG...", intgroup = "treatment")`.
- **More complex designs**: time courses, interactions; see the DESeq2 vignette.
- **Gene-set enrichment** (fgsea, clusterProfiler) on the ranked list.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Check your understanding

1. Why must the rows of `coldata` be in the same order as the columns of
   `txi$counts`?
2. A gene has `log2FoldChange = 2` and `padj = 0.3`. How do you describe it?
3. Why include `donor` in the design?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Answers

1. DESeq2 matches them by position. If they're out of order, each sample's
   counts get the wrong labels, and every result is wrong.
2. It looks 4× higher in the treated samples, but the evidence isn't strong
   enough to call it differentially expressed at the usual cut-off (padj < 0.05).
3. Each donor is measured both untreated and treated (a paired design).
   Accounting for donor removes donor-to-donor differences from the noise,
   so the treatment effect is easier to detect.
:::
:::
